questions.question: Which characteristic lets you increase or reduce resources as demand changes?
questions.explanation: Elasticity adapts available capacity to changes in demand.

questions.question: Which two practices reduce the risk associated with credentials?
questions.explanation: Least privilege limits account impact, while MFA adds another verification factor.

questions.question: A preventive policy can block resources that violate a rule from being created.
questions.explanation: Preventive policies block non-compliant actions before they are completed.

questions.scenario: An online store receives unpredictable traffic spikes. Its web tier is stateless and demand can multiply within minutes.
questions.question: Which approach best responds to this pattern?

options.text: Horizontal autoscaling behind a load balancer

questions.explanation: Because there is no local state, multiple instances can scale horizontally behind a load balancer.

questions.scenario: An online store receives unpredictable traffic spikes. Its web tier is stateless and demand can multiply within minutes.
questions.question: Which signal should be used to trigger scaling?

options.text: A load metric, such as requests or CPU

questions.explanation: An observable demand signal lets the system adjust capacity automatically.

questions.question: Match each need with the most appropriate service type.
questions.description: Select an item on the left, then select its match on the right.
questions.explanation: Each service addresses a specific architecture responsibility.

questions.question: The {{rto}} defines the maximum time to restore service, while the {{rpo}} defines acceptable data loss measured in time.
questions.explanation: RTO focuses on recovery time; RPO focuses on the recovery point for data.
